alerts.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 1 at 7:12AM MST until November 2 at 12:00PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected above 10, 000 feet. Total snow
accumulations between 12 and 18 inches, with locally higher amounts
possible. Winds gusting as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Northwest San Juan Mountains and Southwest San Juan
Mountains.

* WHEN...Until noon MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact the Monday morning commute.
alerts.areaDesc: Northwestern San Juan Mountains; Southwest San Juan Mountains

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued November 1 at 5:57AM MST until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected to occur.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Colorado, including the
following areas, the Eastern San Juan Mountains, and the Upper Rio
Grande Valley.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone location.
Rockslides will be possible in the mountainous areas. Highway 160
and Highway 17 will likely be significantly impacted by this storm.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy rainfall is expected to fall today and Monday across the
area, leading to elevated concerns for flooding in areas that
have recently received excessive moisture, or have recently
experienced flooding.
- The greatest risk of flooding will be along the Conejos River and
the South Fork of the Rio Grande, including South Fork and
Mogote.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood http://cotrip.org
alerts.areaDesc: Upper Rio Grande Valley/Eastern San Juan Mountains Below 10000 Ft; Eastern San Juan Mountains Above 10000 Ft

alerts.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 1 at 3:04AM MST until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations 8 to 14
inches. Winds gusting as high as 50 mph.

* WHERE...Eastern San Juan Mountains Above 10000 Feet.

* WHEN...From 5 PM this afternoon to 11 AM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult, especially Sunday night
and Monday morning. Strong winds could produce areas of blowing and
drifting snow.
alerts.areaDesc: Eastern San Juan Mountains Above 10000 Ft

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued October 31 at 10:37PM MDT until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, Animas River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, San
Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains and southeast
Utah, including the following areas, Canyonlands/Natural Bridges,
La Sal and Abajo Mountains and Southeast Utah.

* WHEN...From 5 AM MST Sunday through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, recently burned areas, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Storm
drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- 1 to 3 inches of rain is expected across portions of southeast
Utah and southwest Colorado from Sunday morning through Monday
morning over soils that are still saturated from recent rainfall
and flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
alerts.areaDesc: Southwest San Juan Mountains; Four Corners/Upper Dolores River; Animas River Basin; San Juan River Basin; Southeast Utah; La Sal and Abajo Mountains; Canyonlands/Natural Bridges

alerts.headline: Avalanche Advisory issued October 31 at 7:16PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
alerts.description:
SABCO

THE FOLLOWING MESSAGE IS TRANSMITTED AT THE REQUEST OF THE
COLORADO AVALANCHE INFORMATION CENTER.

...A SPECIAL AVALANCHE ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM 4:30 PM SATURDAY
UNTIL 4:30 PM MONDAY...

*WHAT...Avalanche conditions are dangerous above treeline.
*WHERE...West Elk Mountains, Elk Mountains, San Juan Mountains, and
La Plata Mountains
*WHEN...From 4:30 PM Saturday until 4:30 PM Monday.
*IMPACTS...Backcountry travelers can easily trigger dangerous
avalanches large enough to bury a human.

*PRECAUTION/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...A potent winter storm increases
avalanche danger Sunday into Monday. Rain, snow, and wind will cause
natural avalanches above treeline. Check the forecast at
www.colorado.gov/avalanche.

Beyer & Pritchett

alerts.title: Chain Law Code 18
alerts.description: Between US Basin Brooklyns / 825 (9 miles north of the Silverton area) and Forest Service Road 871 (Ouray) from Mile Point 80 to Mile Point 95. Commercial Motor Vehicles (CMV) must have chains or approved alternative traction devices. Slower speeds are advised.

alerts.title: Traction Law Code 15
alerts.description: Between US Basin Brooklyns / 825 (9 miles north of the Silverton area) and Forest Service Road 871 (Ouray) from Mile Point 80 to Mile Point 95. Passenger vehicles that are all-wheel drive (AWD) or four-wheel drive (4WD) must have winter (Mountain Snowflake icon) or mud and snow (M+S or M/S) or manufacturer rated all-weather tires with adequate tread depth of at least 3/16 of an inch. Two-wheel drive (2WD) vehicles are required to have chains or an approved traction device. Slower speeds are advised.
